faq.q: Why are hummingbird flight muscles so big?
faq.a: Hovering needs a lot of power, so the flight muscles are a quarter or more of the bird's weight, one of the largest shares of any bird. They are packed with mitochondria to burn sugar fast.
asks: How do hummingbirds have enough power to hover?

faq.a: Its wings swivel at the shoulder and sweep in a flat figure of eight, turning over on each stroke so they push air down both forwards and backwards. Most lift comes on the downstroke, but the upstroke helps too.

faq.q: How fast does a hummingbird's heart beat?
faq.a: In flight, a hummingbird's heart can beat over 1,000 times a minute, compared with about 70 for a resting human. Its breathing is fast too, around 250 breaths a minute at rest.
asks: Do hummingbirds have the fastest heartbeat?

faq.q: What do hummingbirds do at night?
faq.a: Many go into torpor, a deep, cold rest. Their body temperature can drop by over 20 degrees Celsius, and their heart and breathing slow down, saving up to about 95 percent of their energy.
asks: How do hummingbirds survive the night without food?

faq.q: How much does a hummingbird eat?
faq.a: A hummingbird may drink about half its body weight or more in nectar sugar each day, visiting hundreds or even a thousand flowers, and eats small insects for protein.
asks: Why do hummingbirds eat so often?

facts: Many hummingbirds beat their wings around 50 times per second while hovering.
A hummingbird's heart can exceed 1,000 beats per minute during flight.

options.say: Eats stored nectar from its nest

quiz.why: In torpor its body cools and slows, using far less fuel until dawn.

wrong.1: Hovering all night would use up its fuel.
